tickets.title: Spike: measure Cloud SQL start time and stopped billing
tickets.summary: Measure stopped-to-RUNNABLE time and confirm a stopped instance bills storage only, recorded as an ADR.
tickets.description:
Overview section 10 item 6: the stopped-to-RUNNABLE time of Cloud SQL is undocumented; measure it. Also confirm stopped-instance billing is storage only (ADR-020: 'The idle estimate assumes a stopped instance bills storage only; unverified').

Build: scripts/spikes/cloudsql_start_time.sh that, against a throwaway Cloud SQL PostgreSQL 16 Enterprise 2 vCPU / 8 GiB instance created with gcloud (not Terraform, same size as ADR-020, with ~10 GB of data and private IP via PSC if the E2 VPC exists, otherwise public IP for the throwaway only), runs N=5 cycles of: patch --activation-policy=NEVER, wait STOPPED, patch --activation-policy=ALWAYS, record seconds until state RUNNABLE and until a psql SELECT 1 succeeds. Then leave the instance stopped for >= 24 h and read the Cloud Billing export / SKU lines for that instance to confirm only storage (and reserved IP, if any) is billed. Delete the throwaway instance.

Output: docs/adr/cloud-sql-start-time.md with the measured table (per cycle: seconds to RUNNABLE, seconds to first query), min/median/max, the billing finding, and a recommendation for the demo-up wait timeout (used by E10-T18). Context for the researcher: the file is copied into decisions.md later.
Out of scope: the demo-up script itself (E10-T17), Terraform for Cloud SQL (E10-T6).
acceptance_criteria: docs/adr/cloud-sql-start-time.md exists and contains a table with 5 measured cycles (seconds to RUNNABLE and to first SELECT 1), plus min, median and max; a file with fewer than 5 rows fails the check `grep -c '^| [0-9]' docs/adr/cloud-sql-start-time.md` >= 5

The ADR states, with a billing-export SKU list or screenshot reference, whether a stopped instance bills storage only; if any other SKU is billed the ADR gives its monthly amount and the idle estimate delta against the 40-55 USD range
The ADR gives a recommended demo-up wait timeout equal to the max measured start time plus a stated margin
After the spike `gcloud sql instances list` shows no throwaway instance (command output attached in the PR)

tickets.title: Spike: worker pool scale to 0 and Terraform support
tickets.summary: Verify a Cloud Run worker pool can be set to 0 instances and managed by Terraform with ignore_changes, as an ADR.
tickets.description:
ADR-019 and ADR-020 list 'worker pool scale to 0 and its Terraform support' as unverified. Verify with a minimal worker pool using the chosen Google provider version from stack.md.

Build: a throwaway Terraform config under scripts/spikes/worker_pool/ that creates a Cloud Run worker pool (google_cloud_run_v2_worker_pool) from a hello-world image with manual_instance_count = 1 and lifecycle.ignore_changes = [scaling[0].manual_instance_count] (check the real attribute path), then: (a) set count to 0 with `gcloud run worker-pools update --scaling` or the documented equivalent and confirm 0 instances run and no billing for idle; (b) run `terraform plan` and confirm no diff; (c) scale back to 2 and plan again; (d) record the exact gcloud command the demo scripts must use.

Output: docs/adr/worker-pool-scale-to-zero.md with commands, provider version, plan outputs, and the result. If scale to 0 or the Terraform resource is not supported, the ADR states the fallback (for example min instance count semantics or deleting/recreating the pool) and that the fallback must be raised as a question before E10-T9.
Out of scope: the real fa-worker pool (E10-T9).
acceptance_criteria: docs/adr/worker-pool-scale-to-zero.md records the provider version and the exact gcloud command that sets instance count to 0 and to N

After scaling to 0 `gcloud run worker-pools describe` shows instance count 0, and `terraform plan -detailed-exitcode` returns exit code 0 (no drift) with ignore_changes set; both outputs are in the ADR
After scaling to 2 `terraform plan -detailed-exitcode` still returns 0
The throwaway worker pool and its Terraform state are destroyed; `gcloud run worker-pools list` is empty

tickets.title: Spike: confirm ALB and Cloud Armor idle prices and Confluent Basic cost
tickets.summary: Confirm the unverified idle cost items (ALB forwarding rule, Cloud Armor policy, Confluent Basic) against pricing and billing, as an ADR.
tickets.description:
Overview section 2.5 and section 10 item 9: ALB 18.25 USD/month is a list-price figure, Cloud Armor ~6-10 USD and Confluent Basic ~0-5 USD are UNVERIFIED. ADR-012 trigger to revisit: 'Cloud Armor cost verification fails the idle budget'.

Build: docs/adr/idle-cost-confirmation.md containing, for us-central1: the external Application Load Balancer forwarding-rule hourly SKU x 730 h, the Cloud Armor policy and rule fees (count the actual rules in terraform/edge/ from E2) and per-request charge at the 2,000-chat demo month, the Confluent Basic cluster hourly/base cost plus ingress/egress/storage for the demo month, and Cloud SQL stopped storage (from E10-T1). Take SKUs from the Cloud Billing catalog (`gcloud billing` / Cloud Billing Catalog API) and the Confluent pricing page, and where the E2 edge and E5 Confluent resources already exist, cross-check against the real billing export lines of the last full day. Sum to an idle total.

Out of scope: changing the architecture; if the total exceeds 55 USD/month the ADR says so and the finding goes to the researcher.
acceptance_criteria: docs/adr/idle-cost-confirmation.md lists each idle line item with SKU id or pricing URL, unit price, quantity and monthly amount for ALB, Cloud Armor, Confluent Basic, Cloud SQL storage, Artifact Registry/Secrets/GCS/logs
The ADR gives a summed idle monthly total and states pass or fail against the 40-55 USD idle range of overview 2.5; a missing total or missing verdict fails review
Each previously UNVERIFIED value (Cloud Armor, Confluent Basic) is replaced by a number with its source, or is marked still unverified with the reason

tickets.title: Terraform v2 root: state, profiles, Artifact Registry, per-service SAs
tickets.summary: Create the Terraform v2 root module with per-env state, demo/prod profile variables, Artifact Registry and one least-privilege service account per service and job.
tickets.description:
Implements overview 4.12 ('Terraform ... owns every resource in this view ... with state per env prefix') and 8.3 ('Service identity: one service account per service ... least privilege; no project-wide secretAccessor (G-50)'). E0-T7 has already removed the MVP LiteLLM/Kong resources; E2 owns terraform/edge/ (VPC, Private Google Access, private run.app zone, fa-gateway, ALB, Cloud Armor, log sink). Reuse those modules; do not recreate them.

Build under terraform/: backend config with a GCS state bucket and prefix per env (demo, prod); variables.tf with `env_profile` in {demo, prod} that selects the Cloud SQL HA flag and min instances (consumed by later tickets); Artifact Registry repo (images referenced by digest only; a variable `image_digest` with no default and a validation that rejects values not matching ^sha256:[a-f0-9]{64}$ so tags and `latest` are refused); service accounts: gateway (E2 may already create it, reuse), chat-api, worker, and one per job (migrate, maintenance, etl, etl-public, dbt, eval, redteam, demo-prewarm, demo-ttl); required API enablement. IAM bindings are per resource (for example secretAccessor on individual secrets in E10-T7/T9), never project-level secretAccessor.

Out of scope: the resources that use the SAs (later tickets).
acceptance_criteria: `terraform init` with the demo and prod backend prefixes and `terraform validate` pass in CI (named job terraform-validate)
`terraform plan -var image_digest=latest` fails with the validation error; with a valid sha256 digest it passes
A script check (`scripts/check_iam.sh` or a terraform test) fails if any google_project_iam_* resource or member grants roles/secretmanager.secretAccessor at project level; it passes on the tree
`terraform plan` lists one service account for each of chat-api, worker and the 9 jobs and no `google_project_iam_member` for secretAccessor

tickets.title: Add org policy check for requireInvokerIam on fa-gateway
tickets.summary: Verify the org policy allows the invoker-check exception on fa-gateway only, and fail loudly if not.
tickets.description:
8.3: `fa-gateway`: 'invoker check disabled (the only service where it is) ... E10 checks the org policy constraints/run.managed.requireInvokerIam.' ADR-012: 'the invoker-check exception on fa-gateway depends on the org policy allowing it (checked in E10)'.

Build scripts/check_org_policy.sh: runs `gcloud org-policies describe run.managed.requireInvokerIam --project=$PROJECT --effective` (and the folder/org if the project has none), parses the effective policy, and exits non-zero with a message that says which scope enforces it if enforcement is TRUE for the project. Add it as a pre-apply step in the Terraform apply workflow (E10-T15) and as a precondition `check` block or documented make target `make check-org-policy`.
If the project is not in an organization (no policy possible) the script reports 'no org policy; invoker check can be disabled' and exits 0.

Out of scope: changing the org policy; if enforced, record it in questions of the PR and stop.
acceptance_criteria: With a stubbed gcloud returning enforce: true, `scripts/check_org_policy.sh` exits 1 and prints the scope (unit test in tests/scripts or bats)
With a stubbed gcloud returning enforce: false or a not-found for a project without an organization, it exits 0 (unit test)
`make check-org-policy` against the real project exits 0, output attached to the PR

tickets.title: Terraform Cloud SQL (PG16, PSC, no public IP, profile HA flag)
tickets.summary: Provision Cloud SQL PostgreSQL 16 via PSC with private-only access, the connection limit flag and ignore_changes on activation_policy.
tickets.description:
Implements 4.9 and 8.3 ('Cloud SQL: Private IP via PSC; no public IPv4 (fixes G-26)') and ADR-020 ('Cloud SQL Enterprise 2 vCPU / 8 GiB ~101 USD while running (HA ~202)'; 'HA is a Terraform flag for load tests'). Read stack.md for the exact PostgreSQL version (16) and the pgvector 0.8.5 note: the extension is created by the migrate job (E1), not here.

Build terraform/cloud_sql.tf (replace the MVP file): google_sql_database_instance, database_version POSTGRES_16, edition ENTERPRISE, tier for 2 vCPU / 8 GiB (db-custom-2-8192), ip_configuration with ipv4_enabled = false and psc_config enabled with allowed consumer project, PSC endpoint (forwarding rule + address) in the E2 VPC subnet and a DNS record or hostname output used for DB_HOST; database_flags max_connections=400; availability_type = REGIONAL when env_profile = prod else ZONAL; deletion_protection true in prod; lifecycle { ignore_changes = [settings[0].activation_policy] }; initial activation_policy ALWAYS at first apply (the demo scripts flip it afterwards). Outputs: instance name, PSC endpoint address. Backups/PITR: see questions.

Out of scope: roles and databases (E10-T7).
acceptance_criteria: `terraform plan` (checked by a policy test, conftest or terraform test) fails if ip_configuration.ipv4_enabled is true; it passes on the tree
Plan output for env_profile=demo shows availability_type ZONAL and for prod shows REGIONAL (two terraform test cases)
After applying, `gcloud sql instances describe` shows databaseFlags max_connections=400 and no PUBLIC address in ipAddresses
After `gcloud sql instances patch --activation-policy=NEVER`, `terraform plan -detailed-exitcode` returns 0 (ignore_changes works)

tickets.title: Create DB roles, passwords and the dagster database in Cloud SQL
tickets.summary: Create every runtime login role with a Secret Manager password and the dagster database in Cloud SQL without secret values in Terraform state.
tickets.description:
Boundary: E1-T3 bootstraps roles and the dagster database for local/CI only; E10 owns creating the roles, passwords and the dagster database in Cloud SQL. Overview 8.4: Secret Manager holds 'DB password per role'; 'Terraform never stores secret values in state in plaintext (G-27)'. 4.8 job table gives the roles: fa_owner, fa_app, fa_worker, fa_maint, fa_etl, fa_etl_public, fa_dbt, fa_eval, and fa_dagster (owns database `dagster`, no access to app schemas; config keys DAGSTER_PG_DB=dagster, DAGSTER_PG_USER=fa_dagster).

Build: (1) Terraform creates empty google_secret_manager_secret resources (no versions) `db-password-<role>` for each role, with secretAccessor granted per secret only to the SA that uses that role. (2) scripts/db_bootstrap.py (run as a Cloud Run job `db-bootstrap` in the VPC, using the Cloud SQL built-in admin user whose password is created/rotated by the script and stored in Secret Manager version, never in Terraform) generates a random password per role, writes a new secret version, then runs the E1-T3 role SQL (reuse the same SQL file, do not fork it) with those passwords and creates database dagster owned by fa_dagster. Idempotent: re-running does not rotate existing passwords unless --rotate is given.

Out of scope: grants on app tables (migrate job, E1), Kafka keys (E5-T13).
acceptance_criteria: `grep -r 'password' terraform.tfstate`-style check: after apply, `terraform show -json | jq` finds no google_secret_manager_secret_version and no random_password resource (test script fails if any is found)

Integration test against a Postgres container: running db_bootstrap twice leaves password secret versions unchanged on the second run (mock Secret Manager client records one version per role) and creates all 9 roles plus database dagster owned by fa_dagster
Against the real instance, `psql` as fa_dagster to database dagster succeeds and `\dn` on the app database as fa_dagster is denied (connect refused or no schema usage); output attached
Each of the 9 secrets is readable only by its owning SA: `gcloud secrets get-iam-policy` for each shows exactly one secretAccessor member (test script)

tickets.title: Terraform chat-api Cloud Run service on the VPC
tickets.summary: Deploy chat-api as an internal-ingress Cloud Run service with Direct VPC egress, startup probe and invoker restricted to the Kong SA.
tickets.description:
Implements 4.5, 8.3 and ADR-019: Cloud Run service `chat-api`, ingress internal, `run.invoker` only for the Kong (fa-gateway) service account via X-Serverless-Authorization, timeout 3600, explicit concurrency, one Uvicorn process per container, Direct VPC egress `private-ranges-only` with a startup probe (ADR-024), secrets mounted per service account from Secret Manager, no secret defaults in code (missing config fails boot). Config keys from 6.6: ENV_PROFILE, DB_HOST (PSC endpoint), DB_NAME, DB_USER=fa_app, DB_PASSWORD (secret), DB_POOL_SIZE, DB_STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_MS, IDP_PROJECT_ID, ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY / KONG_EGRESS_KEY, VOYAGE_API_KEY, MODEL_ARMOR_*, LANGFUSE_*, OTEL_*. chat-api has no Kafka client, so no Kafka variables.

Build terraform/chat_api.tf: google_cloud_run_v2_service from the image digest (variable from E10-T4), min_instance_count 0 in demo and >=1 in prod, max_instance_count variable (default per the pool budget in E10-T20), concurrency variable, startup_probe on the health path from E1/E4, vpc_access with network_interfaces and egress PRIVATE_RANGES_ONLY, google_cloud_run_v2_service_iam_member run.invoker only for the gateway SA, no allUsers. lifecycle.ignore_changes on min_instance_count. Also confirm the fa-gateway module from E2 has ignore_changes on min_instance_count and add it there only if missing.

Out of scope: fa-gateway definition (E2).
acceptance_criteria: `terraform plan` has chat-api with ingress INGRESS_TRAFFIC_INTERNAL_ONLY, egress PRIVATE_RANGES_ONLY and a startup_probe block (terraform test asserting the three attributes)
`gcloud run services get-iam-policy chat-api` lists exactly one binding: roles/run.invoker for the gateway SA; no allUsers or allAuthenticatedUsers (test script)
A request with no ID token from outside the VPC to the chat-api run.app URL returns 403 or 404 (curl in the smoke script, status asserted)
After `gcloud run services update chat-api --min-instances=1`, `terraform plan -detailed-exitcode` returns 0

tickets.title: Terraform fa-worker Cloud Run worker pool
tickets.summary: Deploy the fa-worker worker pool with its roles, Confluent secrets and ignore_changes on manual_instance_count.
tickets.description:
Implements 4.7 and ADR-019: Cloud Run worker pool `fa-worker`, entrypoint `worker`, `WORKER_ROLES` = outbox-relay,silver,contextualizer,indexer,acl-applier,eval-judge,bq-sink, DB login role `fa_worker`, one Confluent service account and API key per service (KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP, KAFKA_API_KEY, KAFKA_API_SECRET, SCHEMA_REGISTRY_URL, SCHEMA_REGISTRY_API_KEY, SCHEMA_REGISTRY_API_SECRET read from Secret Manager secrets created by E5-T13 for fa-worker), GCS_DATA_BUCKET, BQ_DATASET, BQ_MAX_BYTES_BILLED, VOYAGE_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or Kong URL, DB_POOL_SIZE. Build terraform/worker_pool.tf with Direct VPC egress private-ranges-only, startup probe where supported, manual_instance_count = 0 initially in demo, lifecycle.ignore_changes = [the manual instance count attribute found in E10-T2]. Per-secret accessor grants for fa_worker only.

Out of scope: Confluent resources (E5-T13).
acceptance_criteria: `terraform plan` shows the worker pool with WORKER_ROLES containing exactly the 7 roles and egress PRIVATE_RANGES_ONLY (terraform test)
After `gcloud run worker-pools update ... --scaling=2` (command from E10-T2), `terraform plan -detailed-exitcode` returns 0

With count 1, a log query shows the worker booted and logs each of the 7 roles started (command and output attached); with a missing required secret the revision fails to start with a config error (negative test)
No project-level secretAccessor was added; the worker SA appears only on its own per-secret bindings (check_iam.sh from E10-T4 passes)

tickets.title: Terraform Cloud Run jobs with per-job SAs and DB roles
tickets.summary: Define the nine Cloud Run jobs on the single image with per-job SA, DB role and VPC egress.
tickets.description:
Implements 4.8 job table and ADR-019. One image, `jobs` entrypoint. Jobs and DB roles: migrate=fa_owner, maintenance=fa_maint, etl=fa_etl (plus fa_dagster for Dagster storage via DAGSTER_PG_*), etl-public=fa_etl_public, dbt=fa_dbt, eval=fa_eval, redteam=fa_eval, demo-prewarm=none (no DB), demo-ttl=fa_maint. Each job: its own SA (E10-T4), Direct VPC egress private-ranges-only, startup probe where applicable, only the secrets it needs (DB password of its role; Kafka keys for etl, etl-public, eval, per config 6.6 one key per service fa-worker, etl, etl-public, eval). EVAL_TENANT_ID and PUBLIC_TENANT_ID passed to migrate and eval jobs. demo-ttl SA needs Cloud Run admin rights (4.8) limited to this project's services, worker pool and Cloud SQL instance patch, and Cloud Scheduler pause/resume, and Memorystore delete for the demo instance; nothing else. The job code (maintenance E1-T12; others in their epics) is not written here, only the job definitions with args placeholders from those epics.

Build terraform/jobs.tf with a for_each over a local map of job name -> {sa, db_role, args, secrets}. Jobs reference the image digest. Set DEMO_TTL_HOURS (decide value 4 as default variable, see questions) and OUTBOX_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_MIN=10 as env on demo-ttl.

Out of scope: Scheduler triggers (E10-T12).
acceptance_criteria: `terraform plan` lists exactly 9 google_cloud_run_v2_job resources named migrate, maintenance, etl, etl-public, dbt, eval, redteam, demo-prewarm, demo-ttl (terraform test counts and names)
A test script parses the plan JSON and asserts each job's DB_USER matches the table in 4.8 (for example etl-public -> fa_etl_public) and that demo-prewarm has no DB_* variables
`gcloud run jobs execute migrate --wait` (after the E1 migration exists) exits 0 under the fa_owner role against the real instance; output attached
demo-ttl SA role list is printed by `gcloud projects get-iam-policy --filter` and contains no roles/owner or roles/editor (test script)

tickets.title: Terraform SPA bucket and ALB backend bucket wiring

`curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://<alb-host>/` returns 200 for index.html after a manual upload of a placeholder file; the same object URL directly on storage.googleapis.com returns 403
No `allUsers` or `allAuthenticatedUsers` member in `gcloud storage buckets get-iam-policy gs://<project>-spa` (test script), or the exception is documented under questions

tickets.title: Terraform Cloud Scheduler triggers and paused-state drift
tickets.summary: Create the seven Scheduler triggers for the jobs with ignore_changes so demo scripts can pause and resume them.
tickets.description:
4.12: 'Cloud Scheduler: triggers etl, etl-public, dbt, maintenance, eval, redteam and demo-ttl. demo-down pauses all except demo-ttl.' 4.8: maintenance runs hourly while the demo is up; demo-ttl hourly. Schedule expressions for etl, etl-public, dbt, eval, redteam are not given in the arch (see questions); use variables with the defaults documented in the PR and keep the paused state controlled by the scripts.

Build terraform/scheduler.tf: google_cloud_scheduler_job for each of the 7, each calling the Cloud Run Admin API run endpoint for its job with an OAuth token of a dedicated scheduler SA that has run.invoker/run.jobs.run on those jobs only. maintenance cron `0 * * * *`, demo-ttl `0 * * * *`. Initial state: all paused except demo-ttl. lifecycle.ignore_changes covering the pause state attribute so `terraform apply` does not fight the scripts (see questions: the arch lists activation_policy, min_instance_count and manual_instance_count only; this ticket adds the Scheduler state because the demo scripts change it).

Out of scope: job code and the pause/resume calls themselves (E10-T18, E10-T17).
acceptance_criteria: `terraform plan` lists 7 google_cloud_scheduler_job resources named after the jobs; demo-ttl and maintenance have schedule `0 * * * *` (terraform test)
After `gcloud scheduler jobs resume etl` then `terraform plan -detailed-exitcode` returns 0
Triggering `gcloud scheduler jobs run demo-ttl` starts an execution of the demo-ttl Cloud Run job (execution count +1 in `gcloud run jobs executions list`)

tickets.title: Terraform Identity Platform tenant provisioning

tickets.title: WIF and Terraform plan/apply pipeline
tickets.summary: Create Workload Identity Federation for GitHub and the Terraform plan-on-PR and gated apply workflows.
tickets.description:
ADR-021 and 8.3: keyless CI to GCP via Workload Identity Federation, no JSON keys; 4.12: Terraform 'applied from GitHub Actions through WIF (plan on PR)'. E0-T13/E0-T14 already build PR CI (lint, tests, terraform fmt/validate); do not redo them.

Build: terraform/wif.tf (google_iam_workload_identity_pool + GitHub OIDC provider with attribute_condition restricting to the repository and, for the apply/deploy SA, to ref refs/heads/main or an environment), two SAs: `tf-plan` (read-only roles, usable on PRs) and `deployer` (roles needed for apply, Artifact Registry writer, run.admin on services/jobs/pools, scoped as tightly as practical). Workflows: .github/workflows/terraform-plan.yml (on PR touching terraform/, uses google-github-actions/auth with WIF, runs `terraform plan`, posts it) and terraform-apply.yml (workflow_dispatch / main with a GitHub environment requiring approval, runs check-org-policy from E10-T5 first, then apply). Pin action versions by SHA or exact version. The bootstrap of the WIF resources themselves is a one-time local apply documented in docs/runbook-bootstrap.md.

Out of scope: the service deploy workflow (E10-T16).
acceptance_criteria: `.github/workflows/terraform-plan.yml` run on a PR that touches terraform/ authenticates via WIF and prints a plan; gitleaks and a grep for `credentials_json` / `GOOGLE_CREDENTIALS` in .github/ finds none (CI step fails otherwise)

A run triggered from a fork or from a non-main ref requesting the deployer SA is rejected by the attribute condition (negative test: `gcloud iam workload-identity-pools` condition test or a documented failed run)
The apply workflow does not proceed when `make check-org-policy` exits non-zero (workflow-level test with stubbed script)
`terraform plan` on the merged tree has exit code 0 after apply (no drift)

tickets.title: Add deploy workflow: migrate, tagged revision, smoke test, shift
tickets.summary: Deploy images by digest with the migrate job first, a tagged no-traffic revision, a smoke test and a traffic shift.
tickets.description:
ADR-021 deploy order: 'migrate Cloud Run job before traffic, then a tagged no-traffic revision, smoke test, then traffic shift', images by digest only; 7.1: Migration failure -> 'deploy halts before traffic shift'; Bad deploy -> 'smoke test on tagged no-traffic revision: traffic not shifted'; 7.3: 'rollback is a traffic shift to the previous revision'. Boundary: E0 builds PR CI; this is the CD workflow.

Build .github/workflows/deploy.yml (WIF via E10-T14, environment gated), triggered on main after CI: (1) build and push the image to Artifact Registry and capture the digest; (2) update job `migrate` to the digest and `gcloud run jobs execute migrate --wait`; stop on non-zero; (3) update the other jobs and worker pool to the digest; (4) deploy chat-api and fa-gateway with `--no-traffic --tag=cand-<sha>` using digest references; (5) run scripts/smoke_test.py against the tagged revision URL from inside the VPC via a Cloud Run job execution (the services are internal; do not hit them from the runner), checking /readyz and one authenticated SSE-free read endpoint defined in E4; (6) on pass `gcloud run services update-traffic --to-tags cand-<sha>=100`; on fail leave traffic unchanged and exit 1; (7) sync the SPA build to the SPA bucket. Also add `make rollback SERVICE=<name>` that shifts traffic to the previous revision. If Cloud SQL is stopped (demo down) the workflow must refuse to run migrate and exit with a clear message rather than start the instance.

Out of scope: demo-up/down.
acceptance_criteria: Workflow test with a failing migrate (bad migration in a test branch against a throwaway DB or a stubbed `gcloud run jobs execute` exiting 1) ends with no `update-traffic` call (assert in a bats/pytest wrapper around the deploy script)

Smoke test failure on the tagged revision leaves 100% traffic on the previous revision: `gcloud run services describe chat-api --format='value(status.traffic)'` unchanged (verified in a staged run, output attached)
The workflow rejects an image reference that is a tag instead of a sha256 digest (unit test of the script)
`make rollback SERVICE=chat-api` moves 100% traffic to the previous revision; asserted by describe output
With Cloud SQL in activation policy NEVER the workflow exits non-zero before running migrate with a message containing 'demo is down'

tickets.title: Implement demo-down script and make demo-down
tickets.summary: Stop the demo in the exact documented order with a 10-minute outbox drain and forced remainder log.
tickets.description:
Flow 6 and ADR-020 down order: (1) pause Scheduler triggers except hourly demo-ttl, (2) drain: wait for outbox empty and consumer lag 0 with `OUTBOX_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_MIN` = 10 then force (remaining outbox rows are logged and delivered on the next demo-up), (3) worker pool to 0, (4) fa-gateway and chat-api min instances 0, (5) delete the Valkey instance named `VALKEY_INSTANCE_NAME` (outside Terraform state), (6) Cloud SQL activation policy NEVER. The ALB, Cloud Armor, Confluent cluster and storage stay.

Build scripts/demo/demo_down.py (typed Python, shared helpers in scripts/demo/common.py with a thin wrapper around gcloud/Google client libraries and a dry-run mode) and `make demo-down`. The outbox count is read from Postgres via a read-only query run in the VPC by the demo-ttl/ `fa_maint` job path or by a small `demo-down` execution mode of the demo-ttl job image (the script must not need direct DB access from the laptop since Cloud SQL is private); consumer lag is read from Confluent API/consumer-group lag (use the credentials of the E5-T13 admin key held in Secret Manager). Each step is logged with timestamp and is idempotent (rerun after a partial failure continues). Exit non-zero if any step fails; steps never run out of order. After the timeout, log the number of remaining outbox rows and proceed.

Out of scope: demo-up (E10-T18); demo-ttl job (E10-T19).
acceptance_criteria: Unit test with fake clients: the recorded call order is exactly pause-scheduler, drain, worker=0, min=0, delete-valkey, sql=NEVER; an out-of-order call fails the test
Unit test: with an outbox that never empties and a fake clock, the script waits 10 minutes (OUTBOX_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_MIN), logs 'forced remainder: N outbox rows', then continues with the remaining steps
Unit test: if the Valkey instance is already absent, the step succeeds (idempotent) and the script continues

On the real project `make demo-down` ends with `gcloud sql instances describe` activation policy NEVER, worker pool count 0, API and Kong min 0, Memorystore instance not found, and Scheduler jobs paused except demo-ttl; output attached
`terraform plan -detailed-exitcode` returns 0 after demo-down

tickets.title: Implement demo-prewarm Cloud Run job
tickets.summary: Add the in-VPC demo-prewarm job code that calls /readyz and warms pools, since it cannot run from the laptop.
tickets.description:
4.8: `demo-prewarm`, DB role none: 'Runs inside the VPC after demo-up: calls /readyz and warms pools and caches (not run from the operator laptop)'. Job entrypoint `jobs` in the one image. Look at the existing jobs entrypoint dispatcher from E1 to add the subcommand `demo-prewarm`.

Build backend/src/.../jobs/demo_prewarm.py: reads the internal chat-api URL, gets an ID token from the metadata server (audience = chat-api URL), polls /readyz up to a configured timeout (default 120 s, interval 5 s), then issues a small number of warm requests to bring connection pools up (use the readiness endpoint repeatedly with the concurrency equal to a fraction of DB_POOL_SIZE; no LLM calls, no data writes). Exit 0 only when /readyz returns 200; exit non-zero with the last response body otherwise. No DB credentials.

Out of scope: demo-up (E10-T18).
acceptance_criteria: Unit test with a fake HTTP server: returns 503 twice then 200 -> job exits 0 after 3 polls; always 503 -> exits non-zero after the timeout (fake clock)
Unit test: the job never reads DB_* variables and never calls an endpoint other than /readyz (assert on recorded requests)
`gcloud run jobs execute demo-prewarm --wait` after demo-up exits 0 and its logs show the poll count; output attached

tickets.title: Implement demo-up script, Valkey lifecycle and make demo-up
tickets.summary: Start the demo in the exact reverse order, create Valkey, redeploy Kong with its endpoint and print the measured start time.
tickets.description:
Flow 5 and ADR-020 (up is exactly the reverse, D16.13): (1) Cloud SQL activation policy ALWAYS and wait RUNNABLE (record elapsed seconds; wait timeout from docs/adr/cloud-sql-start-time.md of E10-T1), (2) create the Memorystore Valkey instance (shared-core-nano, fixed name from `VALKEY_INSTANCE_NAME`, in the E2 VPC, outside Terraform state; 4.6), (3) deploy a new fa-gateway (Kong) revision with the Valkey endpoint in an environment variable and raise chat-api and fa-gateway min instances (fa-gateway max 2 per 7.2), (4) worker pool manual instance count up (command from E10-T2), (5) resume Scheduler triggers, (6) run `maintenance` then `demo-prewarm` jobs (inside the VPC) and wait for success, (7) print the URL and the measured Cloud SQL start time. Remaining outbox rows from a forced down are delivered by the relay automatically after step 4; log the count at start.

Build scripts/demo/demo_up.py reusing scripts/demo/common.py (E10-T16) and `make demo-up`. Which env var name Kong reads for the Valkey endpoint comes from the E2 Kong config (check kong/ and the E2 fa-gateway module; if not defined, add to questions). Idempotent and rerunnable; the Valkey step succeeds if the instance already exists and is READY.

Out of scope: demo-prewarm job code (E10-T17), demo-ttl (E10-T19).
acceptance_criteria: Unit test with fake clients: the call order is exactly sql=ALWAYS, valkey create, gateway revision with the Valkey endpoint env, min instances up, worker up, scheduler resume, run maintenance, run demo-prewarm; a reversed order fails the test
Unit test: the script exits non-zero and skips the later steps if Cloud SQL is not RUNNABLE within the timeout
On the real project after `make demo-down` then `make demo-up`: `/readyz` through the ALB returns 200 and the script's last output line contains `cloud_sql_start_seconds=<number>`; output attached

The Kong revision created by demo-up has the Valkey host in its env (`gcloud run services describe fa-gateway` shows it) and a request burst over RATE_LIMIT_CHAT_PER_MIN gets 429 (counter stored in Valkey)
`terraform plan -detailed-exitcode` returns 0 after demo-up

tickets.title: Implement demo-ttl job to bring a forgotten demo down
tickets.summary: Add the hourly demo-ttl job that runs demo-down when the demo has been up longer than DEMO_TTL_HOURS.
tickets.description:
4.8: `demo-ttl`, role `fa_maint`: 'Hourly safety net: reads the outbox count and runs demo-down if the demo has been up longer than DEMO_TTL_HOURS (Cloud Run admin SA rights)'. ADR-020: 'An hourly demo-ttl job auto-downs the demo as a safety net.' The job must run the same logic as scripts/demo/demo_down.py (E10-T16), so package the demo scripts into the image under the jobs entrypoint rather than duplicating them.

Build jobs subcommand `demo-ttl`: determine 'up since' from the Cloud SQL activation transition (the time of the last operation START/patch ALWAYS from the Cloud SQL operations API) and from a label `demo_up_at` that demo-up sets on the Cloud SQL instance (add the label write to demo_up.py as part of this ticket's PR); if Cloud SQL is stopped do nothing (exit 0, log 'already down'); if now - up_since > DEMO_TTL_HOURS, read the outbox count (query as fa_maint, count of rows with published_at is null) and call the demo-down routine with the 10-minute drain; log the outbox count read. Value of DEMO_TTL_HOURS is set by this ticket via the Terraform variable default (4; see questions).

Out of scope: changing the drain order.
acceptance_criteria: Unit test with fake clients: up for 5 h and DEMO_TTL_HOURS=4 -> demo-down routine called once; up for 1 h -> not called; stopped instance -> not called and exit 0
Integration test against a Postgres container: the outbox count query runs as fa_maint and returns the number of unpublished rows seeded (3)

On the real project, after demo-up and temporarily setting DEMO_TTL_HOURS=0, `gcloud scheduler jobs run demo-ttl` results in Cloud SQL activation policy NEVER within 15 minutes (drain included); output attached
The job fails the check if its SA has roles/owner or roles/editor (E10-T10 IAM test still passes)

tickets.title: Add security and connection budget invariant checks
tickets.summary: Add a scripted check for no allUsers, invoker exception only on fa-gateway, no public Cloud SQL IP, no secret in state and pool sizes <= 300.
tickets.description:
Epic done-when: 'No allUsers binding on any service; the invoker check is disabled only on fa-gateway; Cloud SQL has no public IP; no secret value in Terraform state; the sum of pool sizes over max instances is <= 300.' Sources: 6.6 DB_POOL_SIZE ('pool per instance x max instances over all services must stay <= 300 of Cloud SQL max_connections 400'), 7.2 connection budget (`max_connections` 400, headroom for migrations, dbt and Dagster; fa-gateway max 2), 8.3, 8.4 (G-27), ADR-012.

Build scripts/check_invariants.py with two modes: `--plan plan.json` (static, from `terraform show -json`) and `--live` (gcloud). Checks: (1) no allUsers/allAuthenticatedUsers in any run service, job, worker pool or bucket policy; (2) invoker check disabled (`invokerIamDisabled`) on fa-gateway only, enabled on every other service; (3) Cloud SQL ipv4_enabled false and no PRIMARY/PUBLIC address; (4) state/plan values: no sensitive attribute from google_secret_manager_secret_version or any value matching a configured secret-name list; (5) budget: sum over services/pools of DB_POOL_SIZE x max_instance_count (chat-api, worker pool count, jobs max parallelism x pool) <= 300, printing the table and failing above. Run in CI (terraform-plan workflow) and by `make check-invariants`.

Out of scope: runtime load.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests with fixture plan JSON: one with allUsers on chat-api fails (exit 1); one with invokerIamDisabled on chat-api fails; one with ipv4_enabled true fails; clean fixture passes
Unit test: DB_POOL_SIZE=10, chat-api max 20, worker 2 x 10 = 220 passes; chat-api max 40 (total 420) fails with the table printed
Unit test: a fixture plan containing a google_secret_manager_secret_version with secret_data fails
`make check-invariants --live` on the real project exits 0 with the printed budget total <= 300; output attached

tickets.title: Verify no Terraform drift across a down and up cycle

tickets.title: Load test with stub LLM at 10 QPS against synthetic corpus
tickets.summary: Run a 10 QPS peak load test with a stub LLM and report p95 against the overview 2.1 targets excluding LLM time.

Epic done-when: 'A load test with a stub LLM runs at ~10 QPS peak and reports the p95 targets of overview 2.1 (excluding LLM time) against the 10k-chunk synthetic corpus numbers (fail if above).' Targets (2.1): retrieval first stage (embed + hybrid SQL) p95 < 300 ms, rerank p95 < 700 ms, TTFT p50 < 2.0 s / p95 < 3.5 s, full answer p95 < 8 s, all excluding LLM time (the stub returns a fixed streamed answer after a configured delay that is subtracted from the report). 7.2 and 4.6/rerank notes: Voyage Tier 1 allows ~5 QPS of rerank, so request the tier upgrade before the run (record in the PR) or run with the rerank step stubbed and state which was used.
